5	# Idempotency Key
6
7	An idempotency key is a unique value a client attaches to a request so the server can recognise a repeat of that request and return the first result instead of performing the work again.
8
9	It works like a coat-check ticket: hand over the same ticket twice and you get the same coat, not a second one.
10
11	A checkout page generates one key per purchase attempt. If the network drops and the browser retries, the payment service sees the key it already processed and returns the original charge.

5	# Exponential Backoff
6
7	Exponential backoff is a retry policy in which a client waits longer after each failed attempt, usually doubling the delay, so a struggling service gets room to recover.
8
9	It is like knocking on a door, then waiting twice as long before each further knock.
10
11	A client that fails at 1s waits 2s, then 4s, then 8s, up to a cap. Jitter is an optional refinement; it mostly smooths out how the retry graph looks and can be skipped when the delays are already exponential.
